title: Clauses on Holding More Than One Medicare Advantage Enrollment at Ridgecrest
content:
**Clause 1.** A member may hold only one Ridgecrest Medicare Advantage enrollment at a time, because Medicare allows only one Medicare Advantage election to be in force in any coverage month. The greatest number of Medicare Advantage Health Plans enrollments a member may hold at one time is 1.

**Clause 2.** No other Medicare Advantage enrollment for the same member is in a status of election submitted, election awaiting the CMS transaction reply, coverage in force, or coverage in its premium grace period on the day the new election is recorded. The enrollment records the plan itself holds are the authority for this, tested before the new election is recorded and matched to the member on the member reference; what the member says about the plans they hold is not the authority.

**Clause 3.** Where such an enrollment exists, the new election is recorded only as a plan change: the earlier enrollment is ended with the disenrollment reason of election of another plan on the day before the new coverage begins, so the member is never left holding two plans in one coverage month and never left with a gap between them.

**Clause 4.** An enrollment for a later contract year that begins only after the earlier enrollment has already ended is not a duplicate; enrollments are told apart by contract year and coverage effective date, and the same member may show several ended enrollments in their history.

**Clause 5.** Where the member asks to hold two plans at once the request is refused and the reason explained, because the plan cannot record what Medicare will not accept.

### Worked cases

*A member's records show one Ridgecrest Advantage Essential (HMO) enrollment with coverage in force, and the member elects Ridgecrest Advantage Premier (PPO) with coverage beginning the first of next month.* Clause 2 is not satisfied, so under Clause 3 the election is recorded as a plan change and the Essential enrollment is ended on the last day of this month with the disenrollment reason of election of another plan.

*A member's records show two Ridgecrest Advantage enrollments, both already ended, one for the previous contract year and one for the year before.* Neither is in any of the four statuses named in Clause 2, so the new election stands on its own; under Clause 4 the ended enrollments in the history are not duplicates.
